newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China seen importing 15 mln tonnes a year of grain.
newsitem.headline: China seen importing 15 mln tonnes a year of grain.

text.p: China will import about 15 million tonnes by early in the next century as output fails to keep up with rising consumption especially in the animal feed industry, Chinese officials said on Monday.

"It is predicted that China will import 15 million tonnes of grain every year," a report by Li Qiong, Chen Qiubo and Zhou Hanlin of the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences presented to a feed ingredients conference in Singapore said.

Grain demand by 2000 will reach an estimated 478.8 million tonnes and rise to about 515.78 million tonnes by 2010 with most of the increase caused by the sharp expansion of the poultry and livestock industry.

Chinese grain production, however, reached only 445.7 million tonnes in 1994 and will hover at around 450 million tonnes in coming years, the report said. China eventually plans to boost grain output to 500 million tonnes.

"The demand for grain...has been increasing with the expansion of the feed industry," it said. "Tight supplies of grain will be a long headache (for China). The grain problem in China is in effect a feed grain problem."
Some of the measures Beijing will take to ensure food security include increasing the amount of land cultivated to feed crops and using technology to raise yields.
